summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, multiple prior stents, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, type 2 diabetes, antiphospholipid syndrome, and prior pulmonary embolism on warfarin was admitted for worsening dyspnea and episodic chest pain radiating to the left arm. Initial evaluation revealed a supratherapeutic INR of 5.7, normal troponins, and mild metabolic acidosis. Due to high clinical suspicion, a cardiac catheterization was performed after INR normalization, revealing an 80% lesion in the mid-LAD and a 75% lesion in the OM1, which were treated with stent placement and balloon angioplasty, respectively. He was bridged with heparin and transitioned to Lovenox and increased-dose warfarin. Metoprolol was reduced due to bradycardia. He improved symptomatically, was discharged home on dual antiplatelet therapy, adjusted anticoagulation, and home medications, with follow-up planned in cardiology and anticoagulation clinics.
